sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Impeccable gives coding agents a vocabulary for design work. You steer with commands like polish, bolder and quieter, review with critique and audit, and a built-in detector catches the generic look of AI-made interfaces before it ships.
sixtySeconds.problem: Without guidance, agents keep producing the same look: Inter everywhere, purple gradients, nested cards and low-contrast text. Impeccable gives specific commands for design changes and checks pages against 62 rules.
whoFor: Developers building UIs with coding agents
Designers who want precise control over agent output
Teams that want design checks in CI
Anyone fixing a page that looks AI-generated
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want to iterate on existing interfaces with clear design commands and automated checks. It's strongest on pages that already exist.
requirements: A supported agent: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI and more

overview: Run /impeccable init once per project: it reads your code, asks what it can't infer and writes PRODUCT.md, which later commands read. Then name a command and a target, such as /impeccable critique the onboarding flow or /impeccable polish settings. Narrow targets give better results.

There are 24 commands grouped as steer (bolder, quieter, distill, colorize, typeset, layout), review (critique for a scored UX review, audit for a technical report), finish (polish, harden, clarify, adapt, optimize), iterate live, and plan and set up. Live mode overlays your dev server so you can cycle through variants of an element.

The slop detector has 62 deterministic rules with no LLM or API key. It runs as a hook in your agent, or from the CLI and in CI with JSON, GitHub annotations or SARIF output. On Codex use $impeccable instead of the slash command.

features.title: Live mode

useCases.title: Pre-release check
useCases.body: Run /impeccable audit and fix P0 issues.

useCases.title: Block slop in CI
useCases.body: Add npx impeccable detect --sarif to your pipeline.

install.verificationNote: Commands come from Impeccable's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

steps.title: Install
steps.body: It detects your tools, asks project or global, and offers the design hook. Accept the hook and reload your tool.

steps.title: Pin a version for the team
steps.code:
git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor

troubleshooting.problem: Hooks don't run in Codex, Grok Build or Hermes
troubleshooting.solution: They need an extra trust step: approve the hook in /hooks (Codex) or run /hooks-trust (Grok Build).
Run /impeccable doctor to find stale context files, unused settings and broken hooks.

troubleshooting.problem: Hook ran though I denied a command
troubleshooting.solution: In Claude Code, installed hooks run outside model approval. Review them before unattended runs.
